issue_paraphrase: Copying a request context (as happens when a request is handed off to a background goroutine or to a handler that needs its own snapshot) silently drops everything the framework had recorded on the original context: errors attached earlier by parsing or validation are gone from the copy, and the set of media types negotiated for the response reverts to empty. Code that was told the copy would behave like the original instead finds a context that behaves as if nothing had ever happened, producing wrong error responses and wrong content negotiation.
fix_summary: Context.Copy() now duplicates the Errors array and the Accepted array into the new context (deep-enough copy so later mutations on either side do not affect the other), instead of only copying Keys and Params. Intended for the author only; must not leak into instruction.md.
notes: Environment tested: bench-base:ubuntu-24.04 (root) + go1.26.8 linux/amd64 + make. parent (2026-06) and fix declare go 1.25.0; Go 1.26.8 builds both. Always run with -test.run filters: the full 'make test' suite fails as root on an unrelated permission test (TestSaveUploadedFileWithPermissionFailed, which expects chmod 500 to block writes) so do not gate on the whole suite. Test file lives at repo root (no tests/ dir). Test run itself is sub-second once compiled; compilation of the gin package is the dominant cost (a few minutes at 1 CPU). No network needed at test time.

issue_paraphrase: When an application trusts a proxy and relies on the framework to compute the real client IP from the forwarded-for headers, it reads only the first value of the first forwarded-for header line. Real proxies commonly append a new header line for each hop, and in that situation the reported client address is the leftmost address of the first line rather than the rightmost untrusted address, so the application sees the wrong IP. IP-based logging, rate limiting, geolocation and allow/deny rules all act on this wrong address whenever more than one proxy has appended a header line.
fix_summary: ClientIP() now joins ALL values of each configured remote-IP header (strings.Join(C.Request.Header.Values(name), ',')) before validation, so multi-line headers are handled exactly like the single-line comma-joined case and the rightmost non-trusted address wins. Intended for the author only; must not leak into instruction.md.
notes: Tested in bench-base:ubuntu-24.04 (root) + go1.26.8 + make. The parent and fix both declare go 1.24.0 in go.mod; Go 1.26.8 builds both fine. The helper constant localhostIP used by the test already exists at the parent (added by #4481, which landed before this fix), so the regression test compiles against the parent tree unchanged. Use -test.run filters; the whole-suite 'make test' fails as root on an unrelated chmod-permission test. Test time negligible once compiled; compilation dominates (minutes at 1 CPU). No runtime network needed.

issue_paraphrase: Responses produced with the framework's raw-data renderer (arbitrary bytes with a caller-chosen content type, for example generated images or downloads) carry no Content-Length header, even though the byte size is known before the body is written. Middleware, caches and strict HTTP clients that expect a declared length see the header missing or empty, so they may fall back to chunked framing, refuse the response, or be unable to size buffers and progress bars correctly.
fix_summary: render.Data.Render() now sets Content-Length on the response header (strconv.Itoa(len(data)), only when the payload is non-empty) before writing the body, so responses of known size are framed with an explicit length. Intended for the author only; must not leak into instruction.md.
notes: Tested in bench-base:ubuntu-24.04 (root) + go1.26.8 + make. Parent and fix both declare go 1.24.0. TestRenderDataContentLength spins up a local httptest server (no external network). The render package builds independently of the root gin package, so this is a small task surface. Use -test.run filters; unrelated whole-suite failures exist under root (chmod permission test). Compilation dominates runtime (minutes at 1 CPU).

issue_paraphrase: With the framework option that case-insensitively redirects or matches fixed paths enabled, a request that does not match any route can crash the entire server process with a runtime panic instead of falling through to the normal not-found handling. The crash only triggers for nodes in the routing tree that have both a parameter placeholder child and ordinary static children, so applications that mix static and parameterized routes are the ones affected. A single mistyped or differently-cased URL can take the process down.
fix_summary: findCaseInsensitivePathRec no longer assumes the wildcard/param child is at index 0: it first scans static children via the node's byte indices (trying exact/lowercased/uppercased first bytes) and only falls back to the last child (the wildcard) when no static child matches, mirroring what getValue() already does. Added guards so an unmatched lookup returns the not-found result instead of panicking on an unexpected node type. Intended for the author only; must not leak into instruction.md.
notes: Tested in bench-base:ubuntu-24.04 (root) + go1.26.8 + make. Parent and fix both declare go 1.24.0. The panic kills the testify process (recovered, repanicked), so at the parent only the first targeted test runs before the binary dies -- expected, the failure is unambiguous. Fix is the largest of this set (~67 source lines) but mirrors existing getValue() logic. Use -test.run filters; unrelated whole-suite failures exist under root (chmod permission test). Compilation dominates runtime (minutes at 1 CPU).
